summary: The non_gaia variant is a code-only FastAPI/CrewAI-style implementation with endpoints for symptom reporting, health data analysis, authority reports, research insights, user recommendations, and health checks. It covers more user-facing API surface than gaia, but it has critical security gaps: a hardcoded default secret and unauthenticated endpoints that expose health-report workflows. It also relies on in-memory storage and simple rule-based logic rather than durable real-time analytics or verified LLM processing.

findings.description: The configuration ships with a hardcoded default application secret.
Health-data endpoints are exposed without authentication or authorization despite handling user symptom reports and report retrieval.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/main.py:28-82 defines /report-symptoms, /analyze-health-data, /authority-report, /research-insights, /user-recommendations/{user_id}, and /health with no auth dependency or credential check.

findings.description: The API supports direct symptom reporting and recommendation retrieval.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/main.py:13-18 defines HealthReportRequest with user_id, symptoms, severity, duration, and notes; lines 28-39 process reports; lines 71-75 expose user recommendations.

findings.description: The system stores reports and analyzes them, but storage is in memory and therefore does not meet durable real-time health data collection needs.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/system_coordinator.py:16-18 comments that health_data_store and user_profiles are in-memory demonstration storage; lines 27-36 append reports to that store.

findings.description: The implementation uses coordinator method calls among agent classes rather than a defined inter-agent messaging protocol with contracts or fallback paths.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/system_coordinator.py:20-56 directly calls symptom_reporter, user_recommendation, and other components inside one coordinator method.

findings.description: LLM integration is declared in dependencies and agent descriptions, but the evaluated code evidence shows rule-based symptom recommendations and no actual model call in the main processing path.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/agents/symptom_reporter.py:35-47 generates recommendations with simple if checks for fever, headache, and cough.

findings.description: The availability and scalability requirements are weakly addressed: there is a health endpoint, but no deployment, queueing, persistence, load handling, or recovery mechanism.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/health_agent_system/main.py:80-82 returns a basic health status; system_coordinator.py:16-18 uses local in-memory stores.

missing_requirements: Data protection according to privacy regulations is not implemented; endpoints lack authentication and the default secret is hardcoded.
24/7 availability is not implemented beyond a basic /health endpoint.
Scalability for many simultaneous users is not implemented with durable storage, background workers, queues, or concurrency controls.
logical_inconsistencies: The README and agent goals describe LLM-powered processing, but the code path shown in symptom_reporter.py uses fixed rule checks.
The system is presented as multi-agent, but coordination is centralized through direct method calls rather than explicit agent communication.
implementation_risks: Unauthenticated health-data endpoints can expose or modify sensitive user health information.
In-memory storage causes data loss on restart and prevents cross-process scaling.
Broad exception handlers return raw exception text through HTTPException detail, which can leak internal implementation details.
